stem: The bouncing back of light from a surface is called __________.
solution: Reflection is the return of light after striking a surface.

stem: According to the law of reflection, the angle of incidence is __________ the angle of reflection.
solution: The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.

stem: A mirror whose reflecting surface curves inward (like the inside of a spoon) is a __________ mirror.
solution: A concave mirror has an inward-curving reflecting surface (a converging mirror).

stem: A mirror whose reflecting surface bulges outward is a __________ mirror.
solution: A convex mirror has an outward-curving reflecting surface (a diverging mirror).

stem: The centre of the reflecting surface of a spherical mirror is called the __________.
solution: The pole is the centre of the mirror's reflecting surface.

stem: The point on the principal axis where rays parallel to the axis converge (or appear to diverge) after reflection is the __________.
solution: The principal focus is where parallel rays meet (concave) or appear to come from (convex) after reflection.

stem: The distance between the pole and the focus of a mirror is the __________.
solution: The focal length (f) is the distance between the pole and the principal focus.

stem: The relationship between focal length (f) and radius of curvature (R) of a mirror is __________.
solution: The focal length of a spherical mirror is half its radius of curvature: f = R/2.

stem: A concave mirror forms a real, inverted and diminished image when the object is __________.
solution: When the object is beyond C, a concave mirror forms a real, inverted, diminished image between F and C.

stem: A concave mirror forms a virtual, erect and magnified image when the object is __________.
options: between the pole and the focus
solution: When the object is between the pole and the focus, a concave mirror forms a virtual, erect, magnified image.

stem: A convex mirror always forms an image that is __________.
solution: A convex mirror always forms a virtual, erect and diminished image.

stem: Convex mirrors are used as rear-view mirrors in vehicles because they __________.
options: give an erect, diminished image and a wide field of view
solution: Convex mirrors provide a wide field of view with erect, diminished images, ideal for rear-view mirrors.

stem: Concave mirrors are used as shaving/make-up mirrors and by dentists because they __________.
options: form magnified, erect images of nearby objects
solution: When the object is close, concave mirrors form magnified erect images, useful for shaving and dentistry.

stem: The mirror formula relating object distance (u), image distance (v) and focal length (f) is __________.
solution: The mirror formula is 1/v + 1/u = 1/f.

stem: The ratio of the height of the image to the height of the object is called __________.
solution: Magnification (m) is the ratio of image height to object height.

stem: The bending of light as it passes from one transparent medium to another is called __________.
solution: Refraction is the bending of light when it travels from one medium into another of different density.

stem: Light bends towards the normal when it passes from a __________ to a __________ medium.
solution: Light bends towards the normal when entering a denser medium (e.g., air to water).

stem: A pencil partly dipped in water appears bent at the water surface because of __________.
solution: Light bends (refracts) as it passes between water and air, making the pencil appear bent.

stem: The ratio of the speed of light in vacuum to its speed in a medium is called the __________ of the medium.
solution: The refractive index of a medium is the ratio of the speed of light in vacuum to its speed in that medium.

stem: A medium with a higher refractive index is optically __________.
solution: A higher refractive index means the medium is optically denser and slows light more.

stem: The law of refraction that relates the angles and refractive indices is called __________ law.
solution: Snell's law relates the angle of incidence, angle of refraction and the refractive indices of the media.

stem: A lens that is thicker in the middle and converges light is a __________ lens.
solution: A convex lens is thicker in the middle and converges parallel light rays.

stem: A lens that is thinner in the middle and diverges light is a __________ lens.
solution: A concave lens is thinner in the middle and diverges (spreads out) light rays.

stem: A convex lens forms a real, inverted image when the object is __________.
solution: A convex lens forms a real, inverted image when the object is placed beyond its focus.

stem: A convex lens forms a virtual, erect and magnified image (like a magnifying glass) when the object is __________.
options: between the lens and its focus
solution: When the object is within the focal length, a convex lens gives a virtual, erect, magnified image (magnifying glass).

stem: A concave lens always forms an image that is __________.
solution: A concave lens always forms a virtual, erect and diminished image.

stem: The lens formula is __________.
solution: The lens formula is 1/v − 1/u = 1/f.

stem: The power of a lens is measured in __________.
solution: The power of a lens is measured in dioptres (D).

stem: The power of a lens is the reciprocal of its __________.
solution: Power (P) = 1/f, where f is the focal length in metres.

stem: A convex lens has a __________ power, while a concave lens has a __________ power.
solution: A convex (converging) lens has positive power; a concave (diverging) lens has negative power.

stem: A lens of focal length 0.5 m has a power of __________.
The total internal reflection occurs when light travels from a __________ to a __________ medium at an angle greater than the critical angle.
solution: Total internal reflection occurs when light in a denser medium hits the boundary with a rarer medium beyond the critical angle.

stem: The image formed by a plane mirror is __________.
options: virtual, erect and of the same size
solution: A plane mirror forms a virtual, erect image of the same size, laterally inverted.

stem: The speed of light is greatest in __________.
solution: Light travels fastest in vacuum and slows down in denser media like water, glass and diamond.

stem: The refractive index of a medium is highest for __________, which bends light the most.
solution: Diamond has a very high refractive index (~2.42), so it bends light strongly, giving its sparkle.

stem: The magnification of a plane mirror is __________.
options: 1 (image and object are the same size)
solution: A plane mirror's image is the same size as the object, so the magnification is 1.

stem: A concave mirror is used in a torch or car headlight to __________.
options: produce a strong parallel beam of light
solution: A bulb at the focus of a concave mirror gives a strong parallel beam, used in torches and headlights.

stem: Convex lenses are used in __________.
options: magnifying glasses, cameras and spectacles for far-sightedness
solution: Convex lenses are used in magnifying glasses, cameras, microscopes, and to correct far-sightedness.

stem: A real image __________, whereas a virtual image cannot.
options: can be obtained on a screen
solution: A real image can be obtained on a screen; a virtual image cannot.

stem: According to the sign convention, distances measured in the direction of incident light are taken as __________.
solution: By the New Cartesian sign convention, distances measured in the direction of incident light are positive.

stem: A negative magnification for a mirror or lens indicates the image is __________.
solution: A negative magnification indicates a real, inverted image; a positive one indicates a virtual, erect image.

stem: The centre of curvature of a concave mirror lies __________ the reflecting surface.
solution: The centre of curvature of a concave mirror lies in front of the reflecting surface.

stem: When light passes through a rectangular glass slab, the emergent ray is __________ to the incident ray.
solution: After passing through a glass slab, the emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray but laterally displaced.

stem: A ray passing through the optical centre of a lens goes __________.
solution: A ray through the optical centre of a lens passes straight without changing direction.

stem: The image formed on a screen in a cinema hall is a __________ image formed by a lens.
solution: A projector's convex lens forms a real, inverted, magnified image on the screen (the film is placed inverted).

stem: The twinkling of stars and the apparent position shift of the Sun at sunrise are due to __________.
solution: Atmospheric refraction bends starlight and sunlight, causing twinkling and the early appearance of the Sun.

stem: Which of the following correctly matches a device with its optical element?
solution: A car headlight uses a concave mirror to produce a parallel beam.

stem: The bending of light as it passes from one medium to another is called __________.
solution: Refraction is the bending of light as it passes between media of different densities.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'Light – Reflection and Refraction' is that:
options: light follows definite laws of reflection and refraction, forming images through mirrors and lenses that can be analysed using formulae, magnification and power
mirrors and lenses form no images
solution: The chapter explains reflection and refraction of light, image formation by spherical mirrors and lenses, the mirror and lens formulae, magnification, refractive index and power.
